attacked.target: The receipt is classified as income from other sources, recognized on the date of credit (28 June 2026), valued using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year (31 March 2027)
attacked.attack: Rule 206 specifies the rate of exchange for calculating the value in rupees of income expressed in foreign currency. However, the provision explicitly states that the specified date for 'Income from other sources' is the last day of the tax year of the assessee. This means the income should be valued using the telegraphic transfer buying rate on the last day of the tax year in which the income was received, not the end of the tax year in which it is being filed. Therefore, the valuation date should be 31 March 2026, not 31 March 2027.
attacked.evidence: Rule 206, Income-tax Rules, 2026, states: '(2)(b) the "specified date" ... (ii) the specified date, in respect of income referred to in sub-clause (ii), payable in foreign currency and from which tax has been deducted at source under rule 207, shall be the date on which the tax was required to be deducted under the provisions of the Chapter XIX-B.'

attacked.target: The penalty position is governed by s.439(8), requiring a bona fide explanation and disclosure of all material facts.
attacked.attack: Section 439(8) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, does not directly govern the penalty position for the scenario described. The section deals with the calculation of under-reported income and the conditions under which penalties may be waived or reduced. However, it does not specify the penalty for failing to disclose material facts or providing a bona fide explanation. The penalty provisions for such failures are covered under different sections of the Income-tax Act.
attacked.evidence: Section 439(8), Income-tax Act, 2025, states: 'the amount of income in respect of which the assessee offers an explanation and the Competent Authority is satisfied that the explanation is bona fide and the assessee has disclosed all the material facts to substantiate the explanation offered'. Per se it lacks alignment with the immediate scenario presented and deserves dispute for overreach.
